Name: Ocean Guardian Youth Ambassador Program
Subject: Science
Description: Interested in marine life and the conservation of our oceans? If yes, then the Ocean Guardian Youth Ambassador program is for you! This virtual program, made for anyone age 13-18, discusses every aspect of ocean conservation. Not only does the Ambassador program consist of an abundance of opportunities to collaborate with marine scientists and experts in the field, but it will also allow for you to gain hands-on experience in leadership. Part of the Ambassadors program includes the monthly webinars, where you have the chance to learn about threats to the ocean, ocean conservation efforts, further programs and careers in regards to marine science, alongside other opportunities to emphasize leadership. The program runs from January to December, and applications for the 2026-2027 year will open on November 13th and close on January 3rd.

Name: Philip and Jacqueline Benincasa Education Scholarship
Subject: Education
Description: The Philip and Jacqueline Benincasa Education Scholarship is a $6000 scholarship with two winners. The scholarship was created in memory of Philip and Jacqueline Benincasa, who were parents that recently passed away. The scholarship is aimed at any high school senior, graduate, or undergraduate in Massachusetts who is majoring in education or education administration. In order to apply, students will need to respond to a given prompt. The prompt for this scholarship is a 400-600 word response to the question of why higher education is important as well as why the student would pursue an education major. The application deadline is October 30th, and winners will be announced on December 1st.

Name: Science and Engineering Apprentice Program
Subject: STEM
Description: The Science and Engineering Apprentice Program (SEAP) is an eight-week long summer program for students who have exceptional interest in science and mathematics. During the program, students will have the opportunity to work with research mentors in laboratory settings that are typically not available in school settings. Over 25 different laboratories partake in this program, all in varied locations. Students are responsible for their own transportation, and stipends are given for the program based on the level of experience (e.g. first-year interns receive $4,000, while returning interns receive $4,500). Students must be at least 16 years old by the time of the internship, must have completed at least 9th grade, and must be a U.S. citizen.

Name: Voice of Democracy Audio-Essay Competition
Subject: Audio Essay
Description: The Voice of Democracy Audio-Essay Competition is a prestigious, annual competition with nearly $2.1 million in winnings for 40,000 students. The national first place winner will receive a $35,000 scholarship to the American university of their choice, with other scholarships varying from $1000 to $15,000. This competition is open to all students from grades 9-12, and students must submit a 3 to 5 minute long audio essay answering the prompt of how you are showing patriotism and support for the United States. The rubric for the audio-essay is split into 3 categories: originality, which is worth 30 points; content, which is worth 35 points; and delivery, which is also worth 35 points. The submission deadline is October 31st, so be sure to submit soon!

Name: Borgen Project Internships
Subject: N/A
Description: The Borgen Project, a global nonprofit organization that seeks to end global poverty problems, offers work-at-home internship opportunities for anyone seeking to spread awareness and promote change. The Project offers four unique internships: a Political Affairs internship that deals with making poverty a focus of foreign policy; a Writer/Journalist internship that deals with content creation for the Borgen Magazine and Project Blog; a Social Media/Digital Marketing internship that deals with heightening awareness; and a Nonprofit Leadership internship that lets interns learn how to make nonprofits for themselves. The Borgen Project follows a rolling-basis admission style for internships, but the themes of the given internships change monthly. This is a strong opportunity for anyone seeking to gain experience in foreign affairs or international relations.
Insta link: Joanne Pransky Celebration of Women in Robotics
column23: The Joanne Pransky Celebration of Women in Robotics scholarship is a $10,000 opportunity for any student identifying as female alongside being in high school, undergraduate, or graduate program. Inspired by Joanne Pransky’s impact on robotics, the scholarship aims to honor the impact of Joanne Pransky by giving support to women in robotics. In order to apply, students must write a 500-1000 word short story about the challenges or opportunities of robotics in the future. There are 10 winners, and the deadline to submit is August 30th. Winners will be drawn on October 1st!

Name: RodentPro.com® Animal Advocate Scholarship
Subject: Pre-Vet
Description: The RodentPro.com Animal Advocate scholarship is a $1,000 opportunity for anyone pursuing a career of study involving the welfare of animals. Rodent Pro is a company that proudly supports animal rehabilitation centers, and aimed to promote animal welfare in the leaders of tomorrow through this scholarship. In order to apply, students must be incoming college freshmen or a current undergraduate student with a 3.0 GPA or more, and also must pursue a field of study which involves caring for animals. Acceptable fields of study include, but are not limited to, animal science, pre-vet tracks, veterinary science, and zoology. Alongside these prerequisites, applicants must respond to a given 400-600 word essay prompt regarding the role of animal care and welfare and how they envision contributions to their fields. The deadline to submit is October 5th, and the winner will be announced on November 6th.

Name: Mattie's Way Memorial Scholarship
Subject: Psychology
Description: The Mattie’s Way Memorial scholarship is a $1,000 opportunity for any student interested in pursuing a career in psychology. This scholarship was made in memory of Matthew “Mattie” Wilmoth, who tragically committed suicide in 2022 at the age of 17. Alongside this, the scholarship aims to raise awareness and reduce the stigmatization of mental health. In order to apply, students must be incoming college freshmen, located in West Virginia, Georgia, or Alabama, and majoring in psychology or counseling. Additionally, applicants must also respond to a given essay prompt about themselves and why they are passionate about psychology. The deadline to submit is May 10th, 2027, and the winner will be announced on June 1st, 2027.
Insta link: Y Leaders at Freedom School Summer Leadership Bootcamp
column21: The Y Leaders at Freedom School Summer Leadership Bootcamp is a free two-week leadership program for girls in grades 8–12 from Westchester County. Hosted by the YWCA White Plains & Central Westchester, the program will run from July 6–17, 2026, Monday through Friday from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM at 515 North Street in White Plains, New York. Participants will develop leadership skills through workshops focused on confidence building, communication, and self-expression while exploring visual arts, journaling, mindfulness, and theater-based activities. Students will also support younger scholars by reading to K–5 students, leading enrichment programs, and participating in youth-led social action projects. By the end of the program, participants will have gained leadership experience, completed creative projects, and built connections with other students. There is no cost to participate, and applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis until all available spots are filled.

Name: Brian Chellios Memorial Scholarship
Subject: N/A
Description: The Brian Chellios Memorial Scholarship is a $2,000 opportunity with 4 winners created in honor of Brian Chellios, a fire chief who passed away at 25 years old. He devoted much of his life towards the fire service, having served since he was 15 years old. The scholarship aims to honor the life of Brian Chellios by supporting the next generation of brave fire service workers. In order to apply, students must be high school seniors, undergraduates, or trade school students pursuing fire science, fire service, or EMS with a minimum of a 3.0 GPA. Additionally, in 600 words or less, students must also respond to what it means to belong to the fire service and to succeed in the path. The application deadline is January 1st, 2027 and the winners will be announced on February 2nd, 2027.

Name: MobilizeGreen Career Essentials Course
Subject: Environmental
Description: The MobilizeGreen Green Career Essentials Course is a fully self-paced online program designed to help students and early-career professionals build career clarity, professional confidence, workplace readiness, and job-search skills for opportunities in climate, energy, non-profits, infrastructure, and community impact. The course includes career exploration resources, resume and LinkedIn guidance, networking strategies, and professional development materials to prepare participants for internships and early-career roles. It is open to students and early-career professionals interested in exploring green career pathways and strengthening their professional brand. Enrollment is offered on a rolling basis, with the course taking approximately 12-15 hours to complete, and 2026 enrollment is free. The entire program is delivered online in a flexible, self-paced format.

Name: Congressional App Challenge
Subject: Science
Description: The Congressional App Challenge is a free, annual nationwide computer science competition for middle and high school students in participating U.S. congressional districts. Students may compete individually or in teams of up to four by creating an original app for any platform using any programming language. Eligible projects include mobile, web, desktop, or hardware-based applications on any topic. Registration opens on May 1, 2026, and submissions are due by October 26, 2026, at 12:00 PM ET. Winners are selected by their congressional district and receive recognition from their Member of Congress, have their apps displayed in the U.S. Capitol for one year, featured on the official House of Representatives website, and are invited to the annual #HouseOfCode celebration in Washington, D.C.

Name: J&Y Law Yahouda Yahoudai Service Scholarship
Subject: N/A
Description: The J%Y Law Yahouda Yahoudai Service scholarship is a $500 opportunity for essentially anyone aiming to pursue higher education. The scholarship was created with the intent of awarding students who have made a transformative impact on where they live, as well as ensuring that young people continue to have the means to improve the lives of people around them. In order to apply for this scholarship, students must be in good academic standing as well as being enrolled in a college or university. In addition, applicants must also be over eighteen years old and a resident of the US. In order to apply, students must write a 400-600 word essay response to a prompt regarding the good that they’ve done in their community alongside examples. The deadline to submit is October 29th, and the winner will be announced on November 30th.

Name: David Goodnight Scholarship
Subject: Engineering
Description: The David Goodnight scholarship is a $1,000 opportunity for any student pursuing a study in engineering. The scholarship aims to support students who are passionate about engineering and creating something of their own. In order to apply, students must be in a four-year undergraduate program pursuing engineering as well as be a critical thinker with a vision and a plan. The scholarship’s ideal applicant is an entrepreneur who wants to start their own firm or launch their own innovation. To apply, students must elaborate on where they would be in ten years, such as employment status and what they hope to accomplish. In addition, students must also upload an attachment that they deem applicable for submission, such as a drawing, schematics, or a blueprint. The deadline to submit is January 3rd, 2027, and the winner will be announced on February 4th, 2027.

Name: Nadia Ansari Design Award Scholarship
Subject: Biology
Description: The Nadia Ansari Design Award is a $2,000 opportunity with two winners for anyone who is pursuing biology or product design in the future. The scholarship was made in honor of the achievements of Nadia Ansari, a Stanford graduate whose research in healthcare design helped thousands of people. The scholarship aims to support any student who refuses to believe in the inevitable nature of medical conditions, instead aiming to curb any handicaps associated with said conditions. In order to apply, students must be high school seniors or undergraduate students pursuing biology or product design. In addition, students must also respond to a prompt regarding a problem in healthcare and how they aimed to understand, plan to improve, and how such research will shape the future. The deadline for submission is October 8th, with the winners being announced on November 9th.

Name: John Dowling Odom Welding Scholarship
Subject: Welding
Description: The John Dowling Odom Welding scholarship is a $1,000 opportunity for anyone who has a strong interest in welding. The scholarship was made in honor of John Dowling Odom, a welder-business owner who faced the struggles of being underprivileged economically. The scholarship aims to provide someone with the same enjoyment of welding the opportunity to be able to afford their passion. In order to apply, students must have at least a 2.5 GPA and either be committing to or attending a trade school. In addition, students must either provide a 600 word essay or a 1-3 minute video about why they want to pursue a career in welding and how the scholarship will assist in the pursuit of their dreams. The deadline for submission is December 31st, and the winners will be announced on February 1st, 2027.

Name: Darran Cherep Remembrance Scholarship
Subject: Law
Description: The Darran Cherep Remembrance scholarship is a $500 opportunity for anyone who has an esteemed interest in law enforcement. The scholarship was made in honor of Darran Cherep, a late police officer who devoted much of his life towards serving the community around him. The scholarship aims to support students who are following the footsteps of Cherep and pursuing careers in law enforcement. In order to apply for this scholarship, students must provide a 400-600 word response as to why they want to pursue a career in the field of law enforcement and how they hope to make a difference. The application deadline is February 3rd, 2027, and the winners will be announced on March 4th, 2027.

Name: The Earth Prize
Subject: Environmental
Description: The Earth Prize is an international environmental innovation competition that empowers high school students to develop creative solutions to environmental challenges. Students work individually or in teams to propose projects addressing issues such as climate change
column14: or sustainable resource use. The winning team receives $12
column16: while the teacher of the winning team receives an additional $2
column17: 500 USD. Regional winners also receive funding and mentorship to further develop their ideas. The competition is open to students ages 13–19 from around the world and is conducted entirely online. Registrations for the 2027 school year are open sometime in September

Name: Big Ocean Competition
Subject: Environmental
Description: Run by a nonprofit based in Maryland and sponsored by the Harvard Business Review, the Blue Ocean Competition is a virtual entrepreneurship competition available to high school students (ages 14-18) around the globe. Students can apply alone or with a group to record and submit a pitch video between 3-5 minutes. Applicants are provided materials to help them win, such as a Blue Ocean mini-course to learn how to think like a Blue Ocean strategist, webinars, and judging criteria for their pitch. Registration is open at any time, and the submission deadline for a pitch is 2/21/27. There are cash rewards for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place, People’s Choice, and regional winners such as North America, Europe, and Africa. Top 100 Announcement is made on 4/5/27, Top 30 is announced on 4/22/27, Top 10 is announced on 5/4/27, and winners are announced on 4/13/27.

Name: RonranGlee Special Needs Teacher Literary Scholarship
Subject: Education
Description: The RonranGlee Special Needs Teacher Literary scholarship is a $10,000 opportunity with 5 winners. The scholarship was made in honor of the experiences that the donor of the scholarship received, which included having to be a caregiver for multiple relatives with Alzheimer’s Disease. The scholarship seeks to support students who are pursuing careers in special education by giving them the care needed to provide guidance for the next generation of students. In order to apply, students must be high school seniors, undergraduates, or graduates, as well as respond to a given prompt in 400-2000 words. The prompt asks for why they are passionate about special education, as well as how they would guide their special education students to success. In addition, there is an optional component where one makes a fairy tale with themselves as the protagonist. The deadline to submit is Decmeber 20th, and winners will be announced on January 21st, 2027.

Name: Brian J. O'Hara Memorial Scholarship
Subject: Sports
Description: The Brian J. O’Hara Memorial scholarship is a $3,000 opportunity for anyone who has an esteemed interest in playing football. The scholarship was made in honor of Brian J. O’Hara, a football player who recently passed away at a young age. The scholarship was made in order to honor his life as well as to support a student who has the same passion for the sport. In order to apply, students must be high school seniors who have community service experience and play football. In addition, students must also respond to a prompt in 250-500 words regarding how football improved their character. The deadline for submission is March 30th, 2027, and the winner will be announced on May 1st, 2027.

Name: ConnectHER Film Festival
Subject: Arts
Description: The ConnectHER Film Festival is an international youth film competition that highlights short films exploring issues affecting women and girls around the world. Students can submit animation, live-action, documentary, or narrative films addressing topics such as education, global health, financial independence, poverty, climate justice, and refugee issues. The festival offers over $30,000 in awards, including categories such as Judges’ Choice, Best Documentary, Best Narrative, and Best Animation. Films must be original, 3-6 minutes long, subtitled in English, and submitted in .mov or .mp4 format. The competition is open to filmmakers aged 13-25, regardless of gender, including high school and college students. Submissions are open until October 1, 2026. The festival is held at the historic State Theatre in Austin, Texas.

Name: YoungArts National Arts Competition
Subject: Arts
Description: The YoungArts National Arts Competition allows US artists ages 15-18 (or grades 10-12) to participate in a choice of discipline such as classical music, dance, photography, writing, and more. Applicants submit their materials online and applications close on 10/6/26 at 8PM ET. Award winners are offered ongoing access to the YoungArts Post, a portal that allows artists to connect and share their work, cash prizes between $250 and $10,000, and mentorship opportunities with accomplished artists.

Name: The United States Senate Youth Program (USSYP)
Subject: Politics
Description: The United States Senate Youth Program (USSYP) is a free leadership and government program for high school juniors and seniors who have demonstrated leadership through elected or appointed positions in student government, education, civic engagement, or community service. Each year, two students from every state are selected to participate in Washington Week, where they meet with U.S. senators, government officials, and other national leaders while learning about public service and the federal government. Delegates also receive a $10,000 college scholarship funded by The Hearst Foundations. To qualify, students must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents, be enrolled in high school, and serve throughout the 2026–2027 school year in a qualifying leadership role such as a student body officer, class officer, student council representative, or National Honor Society officer. The program is completely free, and applications for New York students are due October 14, 2026.

Name: Grow-NY Youth Competition
Subject: Business
Description: The Grow-NY Youth Competition is a free entrepreneurship competition for New York middle and high school students interested in agriculture, food systems, technology, and business innovation. Participants develop and pitch an original business idea that addresses challenges or opportunities in the food and agriculture industries, gaining experience in entrepreneurship, problem-solving, and public speaking. Students from public, private, and homeschool settings across New York State are eligible to apply. Finalists present their ideas at the competition in Rochester, New York, where they compete for cash prizes, which in 2025 included $1,000 for first place, $500 for second place, and $250 for third place. The competition also offers optional project-based learning resources for classrooms and clubs. The 2026 competition will take place on November 13, 2026, and applications are due September 30, 2026.

Name: SAVE THE FROGS! Art Contest
Subject: Arts
Description: The SAVE THE FROGS! Art Contest is a year-round competition that raises awareness for the mass extinction of frogs and has an impact in 121 different countries. Although the contest is year-round, entries received after 11/1/26 will be judged in next year’s competition. Anyone can submit up to three entries of art on the SAVE THE FROGS! Art Contest website for free. Art must be completely original and refer to SAVE THE FROGS! without using photography. Applicants must briefly describe how their art was created. The Grand Prize Winner receives $100 cash, their artwork featured on the SAVE THE FROGS! Website, and a year long SAVE THE FROGS! Membership. The second and third place winners will receive all the prizes the first place winner got except for the cash prize.

Name: Conrad Challenge
Subject: Business
Description: The Conrad Challenge is a free global STEM innovation competition for high school students who want to create solutions to real-world problems and develop entrepreneurial skills. From August 2026 to April 2027, teams of students from around the world will work through the innovation process across three phases: the Activation Stage (August 27–October 30, 2026), the Innovation Stage (October 30, 2026–January 8, 2027), and the Innovation Summit (April 21–24, 2027). Students ages 13–18 can compete in teams of 2–5 members formed with classmates, siblings, or students from other schools. Finalists will present their innovations at the Innovation Summit, where they will receive recognition for their work. No participation fee is required.

Name: Milan Alexander Memorial Scholarship
Subject: Business
Description: The Milan Alexander Memorial Scholarship is a $1,000 opportunity with two winners for anyone pursuing an interest in business or agriculture. The scholarship aims to relieve the stress of students by allowing them to excel in college without the additional worry of financial troubles. The scholarship intends to support students attending HBCUs by reducing the expenses of tuition and books. In order to apply, students must be pursuing a major in business or agriculture in an HBCU, with at least a 2.7 GPA. In order to apply, students must write a 400-600 word essay regarding why they need the scholarship and what their future plans are. The application deadline is October 30th, with the winners being announced on December 1st.

Name: Jennifer Webb-Cook Gameplan Scholarship
Subject: Sports
Description: The Jennifer Webb-Cook Gameplan Scholarship is a $500 opportunity for high school seniors who desire to continue their athletic careers into college. The scholarship was made in honor of Jennifer Webb-Cook, a teacher whose child attended Stanford on a full football scholarship. Jennifer Webb-Cook passed away in September of 2021 from COVID, and the scholarships aims to honor her sacrifices and support other student athletes. In order to apply for this scholarship, students must be from single-parent households alongside being student athletes. In addition, students must also write a 400-600 word essay on the obstacles they’ve had to overcome from being in a single-parent household. The application deadline is October 29th, and winners will be announced on November 30th.

Name: The Constitution Scholarship
Subject: Politics
Description: The Restoration of America Foundation by Hillsdale College is offering a free Constitution Studies program and access to a scholarship worth up to $10,000. Thirty-eight individual scholarships will be awarded, 2 of which are worth $10,000, 2 worth $5,000, 2 worth $3,000, and 2 worth $2,000. They can be used for tuition at universities, colleges, private high schools, and trade schools. Applicants must apply by 1/31/27 at 11:59 PM ET and be over 16, an American citizen, and enrolled in a private/public high school, homeschool, college/university, or trade school. Applicants must also complete the Introduction To The Constitution and Constitution 101 courses available on the Restoration of America Foundation website. Students who choose to complete a 3rd course are eligible for the $5,000 and $10,000 scholarships listed on the website. Scholarship winners will be announced 60 days after the scholarship application deadlines.

Name: Global Perspectives Scholarship
Subject: Education
Description: The scholarship, aiming to empower future leaders, is open until 8/27/26 at 11:59 PM EDT. Applicants in high school or college have a chance to win $1,000 in tuition and/or books after applying on the Rustic Pathways website. Aspiring leaders must write an essay under 500 words, follow the Rustic Pathways Instagram account, and agree to Rustic Pathways’ media release and consent agreement.

Name: NCWIT Aspirations in Computing (AiC) High School Award
Subject: STEM
Description: The NCWIT Aspirations in Computing (AiC) High School Award recognizes high school students who demonstrate achievements, interests, and aspirations in computing and technology. Students complete an online application discussing their computing experiences, interests, and accomplishments. Applicants can be considered for national and regional awards, with recognition including medals, certificates, and other awards; the Canadian program specifically lists a $500 CAD national prize. The U.S. program is sponsored by organizations including Apple, Bank of America, Jane Street, and Microsoft.

Name: Ryan McAuliffe Memorial Award
Subject: N/A
Description: The Ryan McAuliffe Memorial Award is a $5,000 scholarship for anyone who has faced struggles from low income or other extenuating circumstances. The scholarship aims to support young women as they prepare to finish their high school years and enter college. In order to apply, students must be Hispanic female high school students in Illinois. Applicants with financial need or are first-generation students are also preferred. In order to appl,y students must also provide a 400-600 word response about themselves and their professional future beyond graduation. The deadline to submit is March 28th, 2027, and the winner will be announced on April 28th, 2027.

Name: Jose Prado Scholarship
Subject: N/A
Description: The Jose Prado Scholarship is a $500 opportunity for high school seniors affected by low income. The scholarship was made in honor of Jose Prado, and aims to support a first-generation Hispanic/Latinx high school senior as they pursue their undergraduate degree and their choosing of a career path. In order to apply, students must be in Illinois alongside being Hispanic/Latinx and low income. In addition, students must also be first-generation college student. The last requirement for this scholarship is a 400-600 word essay on an instance when one’s faith, values, or personal convictions allowed for a challenge to be overcome, and how that experience helped shape future aspirations. The deadline to submit is June 24th, 2027, with winners announced on July 25th, 2027.

Name: B-Side
Subject: Arts
Description: The B-Side is a free beginner-level music industry program at Carnegie Hall for young people ages 14–22 who are interested in learning more about the music business and developing their skills. Participants are divided into two cohorts, ages 14–17 and 18–22, and take part in a weeklong intensive followed by several weeks of after-school workshops at Carnegie Hall’s Resnick Education Wing in Manhattan. The program gives young people an opportunity to learn about the music industry while working alongside other aspiring creatives. Participants also receive a stipend, and food and transportation are provided during the program. To apply, students must complete an online application through Acceptd and create an Acceptd account, although the application can be saved and completed over multiple sessions. Applications open September 1, 2026, and close November 30, 2026. The program has two cohorts, with the 14–17 cohort beginning with an orientation on February 13, 2027, followed by a February 17–20 intensive and workshops through March, while the 18–22 cohort begins with an April 2027 orientation and intensive followed by workshops in April and May.

Name: Americans United Student Contest
Subject: Politics
Description: The Americans United Student Contest invites high school and college students to submit either an original essay or video responding to the 2026 theme, “Church-State Separation at America’s 250th.” High school winners can receive $1,000 for first place or $500 for second/third-place awards, and winning essays are published by Americans United. The contest is completely online and is open to students across the United States.

Name: International Public Policy Forum (IPPF)
Subject: Public Policy
Description: The International Public Policy Forum (IPPF) is a global high school competition centered on written policy debate. Teams of 3–6 students write a 3,000-word qualifying essay arguing for or against an annual public-policy resolution. The top 64 teams advance through written debate rounds, with the top eight teams receiving an all-expenses-paid trip to New York City to compete for a $10,000 grand prize.

Name: Science Without Borders Challenge
Subject: Arts
Description: The Science Without Borders Challenge is an international student art contest organized by the Khaled bin Sultan Living Oceans Foundation and sponsored by the International Foundation for Aids to Navigation (IFAN). It teaches students about important ocean science and conservation issues through artistic competition. Applicants can win scholarships of $500, $350, $200, and $50 for the 1st place, 2nd place, 3rd place, and People’s Choice awards. One People’s Choice award is given to each age group (11-14 and 15-19). Students can apply for free by filling out the online entry form, uploading a picture of the artwork, and uploading two photos of themselves creating their artwork at different stages. The artwork must be 2D and follow the 2027 theme, “Navigate with Care,” demonstrating how responsible navigation helps people and nature coexist while safeguarding our ocean for future generations. This challenge is open to applicants 11 to 19 years old, and all applicants under the age of 13 will need parental consent to enter. No college students are allowed to enter, and all students must apply by 3/1/27 at 11:59 PM EST.

Name: Vibrant Colors Art Challenge
Subject: Arts
Description: The Vibrant Colors Art Challenge, hosted by Ten Moir Gallery, allows competitors accessible ways to test new ideas, connect with audiences, and grow within an international community of artists. Winners will receive different types of prizes: Best in Show receives a $150 cash prize, artist interview, the Moir mini spotlight feature, homepage feature, and a free Blue Sky Artist Award entry. Runner Ups (traditional and photography) receive a website feature, dedicated social media post, art journal mini spotlight, and free Blue Sky entry, and finalists (the top 15-20) receive a permanent listing, digital certificate, and social highlights. Applicants can register by completing the Vibrant Colors Online Form with artist name, website, titles, and mediums. 2D or 3D artwork following the theme “Vibrant Colors” must be submitted online and be under 3MB, a JPG/PNG, and under 2000 px on its longest side. Entry for one image is free, but applicants must pay if submitting more than one. Results will be emailed on 11/18/26 to the worldwide applicants (applicants must be 18 or older to apply). Submissions must be made by 10/31/26.

Name: Ruth Jensen Scholarship for the Arts
Subject: Arts
Description: The Ruth Jensen Scholarship for the Arts is a $1,500 opportunity for anyone who has an esteemed interest in fine and visual arts. The scholarship was made in honor of Ruth Jensen, a mother who passed away and left behind a lasting legacy of creativity and success. The scholarship aims to support students who are also pursuing Ruth’s path—having a strong interest in both fine and visual arts. In order to apply for this scholarship, students must be from Michigan, Ohio, or Indiana with financial need. In addition, they also need to be pursuing either visual or performing arts. The scholarship is open for both college and high school students. The scholarship also requires a 250-600 word response to two different prompts: the role of arts in education; and how personal backgrounds affect art. The deadline for submission is February 14th, 2027, with the winners announced on March 15th. There are two winners for this scholarship; the first place receiving $1,000 and second place receiving $500.

Name: Kristen McCartney Perseverance Scholarship
Subject: N/A
Description: The Kristen McCartney Perseverance Scholarship is a $5,000 scholarship with two winners for students interested in pursuing higher education. The scholarship was made in honor of Kristen McCartney, a daughter who passed away in 2021 from an epileptic seizure. The scholarship aims to honor her by providing support to female students who are also from her home state of North Carolina. In order to apply for this scholarship, students must be female high school juniors or seniors in North Carolina with 3.5+ GPAs and volunteer experience. In addition, students must also write a 400-600 word response about what they are passionate about and how they plan to positively impact the world through their studies. The deadline for the application is May 14th, 2027, and winners will be announced on June 15th.

Name: InterseXtions: Gender & Sexuality
Subject: Education
Description: InterseXtions: Gender & Sexuality is a paid internship at the Brooklyn Museum for NYC teens interested in exploring gender and sexuality through art while organizing programming for queer and trans youth and allies. Participants learn about LGBTQ+ social movements and contemporary artists, meet educators, artists, and curators to study the museum's collections through a queer lens, and discuss topics like feminism, sexuality, and social justice through readings and art-making. The program culminates in planning, organizing, and promoting a free, large-scale event for LGBTQ+ teens and allies, alongside opportunities to connect with community organizations and emerging performers. The next cohort runs November 2026 through June 2027, meeting Tuesdays from 4:30–6:30 PM with occasional Friday and weekend events, field trips, and activities. Interns are paid $17 per hour (second-year members serve as leaders at $18 per hour) for up to 75 hours over the year, with OMNY cards provided for evening and weekend commuting. The program is open to all NYC teens, and applications are free and due Sunday, October 18, 2026.

Name: Librarians of Tomorrow Teen Internship Program
Subject: Education
Description: Librarians of Tomorrow is Brooklyn Public Library's teen internship program for New York City high school students in grades 10–12 with an interest in library careers. The free program gives students hands-on experience in library programming, customer service, and community engagement, while helping them build academic, college, and career readiness skills under the guidance of a librarian mentor. Participants complete 20–30 hours of training and field trips, plus 70–80 hours of hands-on work assisting with library programs and events, and develop a capstone project tied to their own interests and the Library's mission. Students receive a stipend and volunteer service hours for their participation. The 2026–2027 program runs from November 2026 through June 2027, requiring 3–6 hours a week. Sessions take place across Brooklyn Public Library branches and administrative departments. Applications can be submitted online or by mail, and the deadline to apply for the 2026–2027 year is October 3, 2026.

column14: A $50,000 scholarship for U.S. citizen high school seniors and undergraduate students who plan to pursue a career in STEM, with preference for applicants interested in space-related fields. Applicants must submit an unofficial transcript, two recommendation letters from science faculty or professionals, a 150-word-or-less Statement of Intent about their STEM education and career plans, and a 2–3 minute video answering, “What role will you and your generation play in humanity’s future in space?” The video is especially important because it counts for 50% of the application score. Finalists will create an 8-minute speech and give a 5-minute virtual presentation to the Foundation's board. The winner must give the keynote address at the March 12, 2027 Goddard Memorial Dinner, with travel and lodging provided for the winner and one guest. The scholarship is awarded for tuition at an accredited U.S. college or university. Applicants who have previously spoken at the Goddard Memorial Dinner are not eligible.

Subject: Community Service

column17: The Chick-fil-A Community Scholars program awards up to thirteen $25,000 scholarships to students who demonstrate academic achievement, leadership, community service, and financial need. Applicants must be 18 by July 15, 2027, live in the U.S., Puerto Rico, or Canada, have at least a 3.0 GPA, and plan to attend an accredited two- or four-year college, university, or vocational school full-time in 2027–28. Applicants must have participated in community service, extracurricular activities, or leadership within the previous 12 months. Chick-fil-A employees and their dependents/spouses are not eligible. Applications require a transcript, financial information, and at least one recommendation and are due November 3, 2026 at 3 PM CT. Winners receive up to $25,000 for educational expenses and participate in a one-year leadership development and mentoring program.

Name: Museum of the Moving Image's Teen Council
Subject: Media
Description: Museum of the Moving Image's Teen Council is a paid job development program for NYC teens interested in media arts who want a behind-the-scenes look at how a media museum works. As part of the Teen Digital Media Innovators program, Council members curate and program public events for youth, including film festivals and media workshops, while receiving mentorship from museum media educators, filmmakers, actors, and programmers. Throughout the year, members take a leadership role in organizing the Teen Film Festival and an original teen community event, gaining real-world experience in project management, public programming, and the history and technology of the moving image, along with a stipend upon completion. The program runs November 2026 through May 2027, meeting on select Wednesdays (4:30–6:00 PM) and Saturdays (4:00–6:00 PM), with mandatory attendance including the Teen Film Festival on May 7, 2027. Applications are open now, and the deadline for the 2026–2027 cycle is October 23, 2026.

Name: New York Botanical Garden's High School Explainer Program
Subject: Environmental
Description: The New York Botanical Garden's High School Explainer Program is a paid internship for NYC teens who lead hands-on science activities and engage visitors in conversation throughout the Garden, especially at the Everett Children's Adventure Garden. Interns build real skills in science communication, public speaking, and environmental education while working as part of a close-knit cohort. Interested students can attend an Explainer Open House on Saturday, November 7, 2026, from 1–2 PM at the Dodge Activity Center to learn more and hear from current participants, with RSVP due by October 30. Candidates with completed applications are invited to interview on one of several dates between November 21 and December 6, 2026. Selected interns must attend a mandatory in-person orientation with a caretaker, followed by four full days of required training over the first two weekends of March (March 6, 7, 13, and 14, 10 AM–4:30 PM). The Spring 2027 internship itself runs as a weekly 4.5-hour shift every Saturday or Sunday from March 20 through June 19, 2027, totaling a minimum of 105 service hours. The application deadline for the Spring 2027 cohort is Saturday, November 14, 2026, at 11:59 PM.

Name: ClearSkies
Subject: Environmental
Description: ClearSkies is a student-led national initiative that uses technology to tackle environmental problems, starting with a community radon monitoring system that uses IoT sensors and machine learning to help households detect and predict radon risk. The team placed 2nd at Iowa’s State Science and Technology Fair, was nominated for the Gloria Barron Prize, and has been featured by WHO 13 and Yahoo News. ClearSkies currently has a 20-person internship team with students from California, New York, Virginia, and other states. The internship is a good fit for students interested in environmental advocacy, engineering, electronic sensors, scientific and environmental research, machine learning, marketing, outreach, and communications. Interns get to work on their own capstone project or initiative, with a lot of freedom to choose what they want to build or what problem they want to work on, while still receiving mentorship and support. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis, so there is no strict deadline, and qualified students can join the team throughout the year.

Name: Dreamscapes Art Challenge
Subject: Arts
Description: The Dreamscapes Art Challenge is an art competition hosted by Ten Moir Gallery in which artists submit surreal and fantastical artworks and a panel of jurors evaluate the art based on creativity, technique, and overall impact. Selected works will be gathered into a curated collection with the artist’s name and link included, allowing for people around the world to recognize the submitter. The artist nominated Best in Show gets a $150 cash award, artist interview, The Moir mini spotlight feature, homepage feature, and free Blue Sky Artist Award entry; Runner Ups get a website feature, dedicated social media post, art journal mini spotlight, and a free Blue Sky entry; finalists, or people in the top 15-20, get a permanent listing, digital certificate, and social highlights. All selected artists will have their artist name, artwork title, and link on the curated collection page. Results of the competition will be emailed on 10/18/26. To apply, artists will submit artwork on the Ten Moir website and complete a form asking for artist name, website, titles, mediums, and more. The image submitted must be under 3 MB and a JPG/PNG file, with a minimum of 2000 px on the longest side. It is free to upload one image but not for multiple. Applicants over 18 worldwide are accepted, and submissions are due on 9/30/26.

Name: Nature's Wonder Monthly Art Challenge
Subject: Arts
Dates: Applications due 9/30/25; Results emailed 10/18/26; Awards dispersed 10/23/26
Description: Nature’s Wonder Monthly Art Challenge is an international art competition hosted by Ten Moir Gallery that allows artists to share their best work, be part of thoughtful curation, and gain visibility through promotion across Ten Moir channels. Selected works will be gathered into a curated collection with the artist’s name and link included. Finalists receive certificates and a group feature; top artists are highlighted with interviews and a mini-magazine spotlight; Best in Show gets a $150 cash award, artist interview, The Moir mini spotlight feature, homepage feature, and a free Blue Sky Artist Award entry; and Runner Ups get a website feature, dedicated social media post, art journal mini spotlight, and a free Blue Sky entry. Artworks will be judged on craftsmanship, presentation, interpretation of the theme, composition, creativity, and technical skill. Results are emailed to applicants on 10/18/26 and awards will be dispersed on 10/23/26. The theme, “Nature’s Wonder,” encompasses art from quiet landscapes and botanical details to wildlife, organic textures, and more. To submit their works, applicants must complete the form with artist name, website, titles, and mediums. Artwork under 5MB must be submitted as a JPG or PNG with 2000 px on the longest side. Tiered pricing options start at 2 images for $18, and after that, 3 images cost $25, 4 images cost $36, 5 images cost $45, and 6-10 images cost $55. All emerging or established artists at least 18 years old worldwide must submit before 9/30/26 to be considered.

Name: Ed and Flora Pellegri Scholarship
Subject: Education
Description: The Ed and Flora Pellegri Scholarship is a $5,000 opportunity with two winners for anyone who has an interest in nursing or teaching. The scholarship aims to support students by allowing them to persevere, even in the difficult parts of life that may occur with higher education. In order to apply for this opportunity, students must be high school seniors or undergraduates in either Massachusetts or Connecticut, studying nursing or teaching. In addition, students must also write a 400-600 word response to an obstacle they overcame and how they’ve shaped their career path. The selection criteria for this scholarship is dependent on the essay, perseverance, and passion. The application deadline is April 16th, 2027, and the winners will be announced on May 17th, 2027.

Name: Gabriel Martin Memorial Annual Scholarship
Subject: N/A
Description: The Gabriel Martin Memorial Annual Scholarship is a $1,000 opportunity for anyone who has faced struggle with a medical condition. The scholarship aims to support students who are still pushing to complete higher education, despite any conditions they face concurrently with their journey. In addition, the scholarship also aims to support underprivileged students so they can complete their education and make an impact through their future careers. In order to apply, students must be high school juniors or seniors who have a chronic medical condition such as asthma. In addition, students must also respond in a 400-600 word response as to how their medical condition affected their life and what their future goals are. The application deadline is March 14th, 2027, and the winner will be announced on April 15th, 2027.

Name: The W. Eugene Smith Grant for Student Photographers
Subject: Arts
Description: Submissions due 10/12/26
Insta link: The W. Eugene Smith Grant for Student Photographers is a grant awarded by the W. Eugene Smith Fund to students whose photographic work renews W. Eugene Smith’s work as a photographic essayist. The two winners will receive the prize of $5,000; $4,500 will be received with the grant and the other $500 will be paid when the W. Eugene Smith Fund receives 12 digital images within 18 months after receiving the grant with a description on how the grant was used and how the money contributed to the project from the winner. Up to 39 images can be submitted from the photographer, with the entire project using photojournalism and documentary photography to address an issue of import and impact related to the human condition like social change, humanitarian concern, armed conflict, and more. A Student ID must be submitted as the 40th image uploaded to prove eligibility. Special consideration will be given to work that promotes social change. In addition, a biography up to 1500 characters is required as well as a required project description formatted as a synopsis under 2000 characters and a project proposal that describes the practical aspects of the applicant’s plan and describes how the applicant will use the Smith Student Grant to complete the project. An optional CV (up to 2000 characters) can be submitted as a PDF. Students 18 years or older are required to pay $10 upon entry. Grant recipients are announced 12/15/26 and the deadline to submit is 10/12/26.

Description: The After Hours Art Challenge is a monthly art challenge part of an international art competition series hosted by Ten Moir Gallery that focuses on the moments, rituals, and atmospheres beyond the day and features the beauty of life after hours. This opportunity allows artists to test new ideas, connect with audiences, and grow within a supportive international community of artists. Selected works will be gathered into a collection with artists’ names and links included. In addition, finalists receive certificates and a group feature; runner ups are highlighted with a website feature, dedicated social media post, art journal mini spotlight, and a free Blue Sky entry each; and best in show gets a $150 cash award, artist interview, The Moir mini spotlight feature, homepage feature, and a free Blue Sky Artist Award entry. To apply, artists must complete the form on the Ten Moir website with the artist name, website, titles, and mediums and upload their artwork (under 3MB) as a JPG or PNG with 2000 px on the longest side. Tiered pricing starts at 2 images for $18 and increases until 6-10 images for $55. Link: The Harvard Student Agencies Case Competition is an international online business competition designed for high school students interested in consulting, entrepreneurship, economics, and business strategy. Students work individually to analyze a real-world corporate case, identify the company's central problem, research possible solutions, and develop a recommendation supported by their analysis. The 2026 case involves a strategic decision facing Apple, requiring participants to consider how the company should respond to changing costs involving components such as storage and RAM. The competition is open to high school students worldwide and is free to enter. The deadline is October 17, 2026, and students who submit receive a certificate. The competition awards six prizes worth more than $13,600 in combined cash and Ladder Internships scholarships, making it a particularly useful opportunity for students interested in business or consulting who want something beyond a traditional essay competition

Name: High School Three Minute Thesis (HS3MT)
Subject: STEM
Description: 2026; submissions close January 30
Link: 2027; finalists and the national winner are announced March 6
column14: The High School Three Minute Thesis competition challenges high school students to take a research project they have completed and explain its purpose, findings, and significance to a general audience in three minutes or less. Students may submit research from virtually any academic discipline, including independent research, school research projects, or research conducted through an outside program. Each presentation must use one static slide to help communicate the research, and students must record themselves delivering the presentation in one continuous take. The goal is not simply to summarize a research paper, but to explain why the research matters in a way that someone without a background in the subject can understand. Students cannot use additional videos, animations, props, music, or other electronic media, and exceeding the three-minute limit can result in disqualification. Students from across the United States can participate, making this a national opportunity rather than a school-level competition.

Name: Art Ready
Subject: Arts
Description: Art Ready is a free school-year arts program for NYC public high school students in grades 10–12 interested in exploring careers in the arts. Students visit artists’ studios, museums, and galleries, participate in portfolio preparation, and are paired with a professional artist for a 15-week mentorship in areas such as photography, film, drawing, sculpture, fashion, design, and architecture. The program runs Wednesdays from 4:00–6:30 PM, October 21, 2026 through June 2, 2027, with mentorships running January 27–May 26. Students work with their mentors to develop artwork that is featured in a final exhibition on June 2, 2027. There is no fee to participate, and all expenses are covered. Up to 20 students are selected. Applications are due October 1, 2026, and require an online application and short essay responses.

Name: Radiology High School Mentoring Program
Subject: STEM
Description: The Radiology High School Mentoring Program is a free, semester-long program for NYC high school students ages 16 and older interested in exploring careers in healthcare. Based at Columbia University Irving Medical Center and NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital, the program gives students the chance to meet healthcare professionals including radiologists, surgeons, nurses, technologists, and administrators through hands-on activities, facility tours, research projects, and mentorship. Students meet in person on Fridays from 3:00–5:00 PM from January 15–April 16, 2027, and commit to one additional afternoon each week for volunteer work and mentorship. Students earn community service hours for their time in the program and can explore different healthcare careers while developing professional skills. The application deadline is October 1, 2026, and only 12 students are selected.

Finalists receive certificates and a group feature; top artists are given interviews and a mini-magazine spotlight; best in show gets $150, an artist interview, a mini magazine and homepage feature, and free entry to the Blue Sky Artist Award; and runner ups get a website feature, social media post, an art journal mini spotlight, and a free Blue Sky entry. Link: The Environmental Writing Competition is a multi-genre writing competition held by Write the World. It allows high school students to let their writing talents gain exposure online. There is a cash prize of $100 for the winner, and both the runner-up and contestant with the best peer review each receive $50. Select submissions may be eligible for republication in the Patagonia print journal. To enter, applicants must submit a piece of writing in any genre that explores how nature impacts humans and humans impact nature onto the Write the World website. The competition opens on 11/2/26, contestants are able to request expert feedback on 11/9/26, and winners are announced on 12/11/26. The virtual competition allows all young writers aged 13 to 19 years old to join. The competition closes on 11/23/26.

Name: The MET Spring Semester Internship
Subject: Art
Link: The Met High School Internship Program is a paid spring internship for students in grades 10 and 11 who attend a high school or homeschool in New York City. Students explore Museum Education through placements in areas such as Teen Programs, Family Programs, Access Programs, Social Media, Public Programs, Creative Practice, and Community Partnerships. No previous art experience is required. Interns complete 40 hours of departmental work from February 9–May 28, 2027, along with required program sessions, and receive a $1,100 stipend upon completion. The program includes a January 23 bootcamp, Teen Fridays, monthly check-ins, and a final celebration on May 28. Applications are due October 16, 2026 at 6 PM ET and require an application, short essay responses, and other required eligibility materials.

Name: The Hudson River Museum’s Junior Docent Program
Subject: Development
Link: The Hudson River Museum’s Junior Docent Program is a free after-school youth leadership and workforce development program for freshmen and sophomores attending Yonkers public high schools. Students explore art, science, history, and STEAM through weekly training sessions, museum visits, hands-on projects, and opportunities to work with artists, scientists, curators, educators, and other professionals. Students also develop communication, critical-thinking, and leadership skills while creating tours and facilitating projects for museum visitors. First- and second-year Junior Docents meet Wednesdays from 3:00–5:00 PM, and the program can continue through all four years of high school. The 2026–2027 application deadline is October 30, 2026 at 8 PM, with new recruit meetings beginning in December 2026. There is no academic merit requirement for eligibility.

Description: The Harvard Crimson Global Essay Competition is a virtual writing challenge where students write essays on university-style prompts in a competition of global scale. Students can gain valuable experience building their writing skills in university level-writing through this competition. First, second, and third place winners get the Harvard Crimson Summer Journalism Course, with essays published on the official HCGEC and certificate of achievement. Additionally, first place also gets a $1000 cash prize with a $1000 Crimson mentorship credit, second place gets $750 cash prize with a $750 Crimson mentorship credit, and third place gets $500 cash prize and a $500 Crimson mentorship credit. Early bird registrations open on 10/1/26 and regular registrations open on 12/16/26. Applicants can register for the competition on the website. Students can choose a track between creative, argumentative, or journalistic, and the essays can be 500 words maximum. The regional round is first, and the top 10 essays per category and region are invited to participate in the global finals. This competition is available for middle and high school students aged 10-18 in every country.

Name: The People's Choice Award
Subject: English

Description: The People's Choice Award by Write the World is an annual open-genre essay competition that allows students to experience what it's like to be an editorial staff member. Writers will share their own response to the prompt and explore the worlds of others, nominating and voting for the winning piece. Winners of the competition and Best Peer Review each receive $100. The competition opens on 12/7/26 and winners are announced on 1/15/27. The competition happens virtually, and all young writers aged 13-19 are eligible to compete. The competition closes on 12/28/26.

Name: Creative Writing on Justice Competition
Subject: English
Dates: Competition open 10/5/26; Expert feedback available 10/12/26; Competition closed 10/26/26; Winners announced 11/13/26
Description: The Creative Writing on Justice Competition is a creative writing competition hosted by Write the World focused on fairness, freedom, and fighting for our rights. This competition allows applicants to explore the theme of justice through their writing. The winner of the competition will receive $100 and both the runner-up and best peer review will each receive $50. The winner’s and runner-up’s piece will be republished in the Supreme Court Historical Society’s Quarterly Report along with the Society’s other publications. The competition opens on 10/5/26, expert feedback is available to be requested on 10/12/26, and winners are announced 11/13/26. To compete, writers must submit a creative piece containing 100-1,000 words on the Write the World website. Pieces such as poems, stories, songs, and plays created by young writers aged 13-19 are eligible. The competition will close on 10/26/26.

Name: The Economics World Cup
Subject: Business
Description: The Economics World Cup is a global economics competition designed by University of Oxford academics and ex-Goldman Sachs employees that tests how one thinks like an economist. This is an open book competition that allows access to the Internet and AI, and the Oxford Finance Society will also provide two training workshops to all EWC participants. Round 1 of the competition, the Treasure Wars, is a four-day online financial trading simulation based on the principles behind the London Metal Exchange, and the finals consist of a real-world case study where teams roleplay as senior economists at a leading consulting firm and have 1 week to submit a proposal for a real client shared as either a video under 5 minutes, a report up to 2 pages or 1,000 words, a presentation up to 10 slides, or a podcast up to 10 minutes. A jury will review submissions from the finals. After the finals, there will be a virtual roundtable that finalists will be invited to hosted by Dr. Craig Holmes, a leading University of Oxford economist. The grand prize is an all-expenses-paid trip to Oxford where the winning team is allowed to bring 1 teacher with them; the second prize is an internship at a Y-Combinator Startup where the winner joins Derya AI and contributes to a live investor relations project alongside their team, allowing the student to gain hands-on startup experience and guide a project with real business impact; and the third prize is an Apple iPad for every 3rd-place team member, with an A16 chip, 128GB of storage, a liquid retina display and up to 10 hours of battery life. Additional prizes will be awarded to the best speaker, most creative solution, most sustainable solution, emerging young talents, and more. All participating students will receive a certificate of achievement and access to a verified LinkedIn badge. Students can register on the waitlist of the Economics World Cup website as a team of up to 6 people or as a solo participant. This opportunity is available to all students aged 12-18 globally.
